channel.description: Latest articles from The Catholic Review (catholicreview.org)

item.title: Vatican hosted its own mini Paralympics half a century before Games’ official start
item.description: More than 50 years before the first Paralympic Games were held in 1960 in Rome, the Vatican had already hosted what might have been the very first international sporting and gymnastics event with athletes living with disabilities.

item.title: ‘Underbelly of the AI industry’: Panel explores data centers’ ecological, economic impacts
item.description: The explosion of massive data centers to handle the increasing generative demands of artificial intelligence have placed high demands on both power and the water used in cooling systems -- millions of gallons per day -- and low-income communities have typically endured the brunt of the air pollution they create. This was the topic of a March 5 webinar, "The Growing Impacts of Data Centers on Our Neighbors and God's Creation," hosted by the Washington-based Catholic Climate Covenant.

item.title: Baltimore Catholics bring voice of migrants to U.S. capitol
item.description: “They ask for help, and all I can say is, ‘I hear you. I hear you,’” said Deacon Seigfried Presberry as he described the phone calls he receives from families after a loved one is detained by immigration authorities.

item.title: Católicos de Baltimore llevan la voz de los migrantes al Capitolio de los Estados Unidos
item.description: El diácono Presberry, coordinador del ministerio penitenciario de la Arquidiócesis de Baltimore, compartió esas conversaciones con un asistente de la senadora demócrata de Maryland Angela Alsobrooks durante las reuniones celebradas en el Capitolio el 5 de marzo.

item.title: Experts: Debates about Zionism, even by Catholics, often at odds with Catholic understanding
item.description: Experts in Jewish-Catholic relations told OSV News that some current public debates about Zionism, including among Catholics, are at odds with the Catholic understanding of the term -- which itself has an array of meanings, as does the word "Israel" itself.

item.title: Colorado diocesan-sponsored clergy peer support, resiliency program believed to be first in nation
item.description: When Deacon Ernie Martinez took on his role as director of deacons for the Archdiocese of Denver three years ago, he brought with him an insight few clergy possess: 40 years of experience with the Denver Police Department, where he witnessed firsthand how peer support could save lives.

item.title: Fear: Destroyer of Lenten works
item.description: It is human to be afraid. But this year, in our Lenten disciplines, let us place all of the fears we're conscious of -- or will admit to -- into the vast depths of the Sacred Heart of Jesus, the Christ, who said, "Do not be afraid, little flock, for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom" (Lk 12:32).

item.title: Pope Leo XIV names Archbishop Caccia papal ambassador to United States
item.description: Pope Leo XIV has named Archbishop Gabriele G. Caccia as the Vatican's ambassador to the United States, selecting a seasoned diplomat to serve as a crucial liaison between Rome and the pope's home country.

item.title: More than a Cup of Coffee (and accepting Lenten interruptions)
item.description: As we were walking, I saw a man who looked like he was on his way to work. He was carrying a paper coffee cup—a beacon to me on my hunt for coffee.

item.title: Visitor breath, sweat and climate change prompt work on Sistine Chapel masterpiece
item.description: hen millions of visitors flock to the Sistine Chapel each year, their seemingly invisible breath and sweat are slowly leaving a mark on this Renaissance masterpiece, according to Vatican Museums officials.
